preconditions.description: The number of distinct scores m is between 1 and 31 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= ai <= 30 for ai in a_list) and len(set(a_list)) == len(a_list)
preconditions.description: The input list a_list contains m distinct integers, each between 0 and 30 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: (stdout == '=(') == (not any(all(ai == 0 for ai in a_list) or all(ai == n-1 for ai in a_list) or sum(a_list) != n*(n-1)//2 for n in range(1, 31)))
postconditions.description: If no tournament exists (e.g., sum of scores is not n(n-1)/2 for any n, or all scores are 0 or all are n-1), output '=('. Otherwise, output a valid tournament matrix.

postconditions.expression: stdout.startswith(str(n)) and n >= m and n <= 31 and all(len(line) == n and all(c in '01' for c in line) and line[i] == '0' for i in range(n)) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: If a tournament exists, output the minimal n (number of vertices) followed by an n×n adjacency matrix where each row i represents outgoing edges from vertex i (1=outgoing, 0=incoming), with zeros on the diagonal.

postconditions.expression: all(any(ai == sum(row) for ai in a_list) for row in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) if stdout != '=(' else True
postconditions.description: Each row sum in the matrix must match one of the input scores (allowing duplicates).

postconditions.expression: all(all(row[j] == 0 or row[j] == 1 for j in range(n)) and all(row[i] == 0 for i in range(n)) for row in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) if stdout != '=(' else True
postconditions.description: The matrix is a valid tournament: binary entries, zero diagonal, and exactly one directed edge between every pair of vertices (i.e., row[i][j] + row[j][i] == 1 for all i ≠ j).
